title: Active learning selected oxidative methane coupling catalysts
summary: The authors combined automatic feature engineering with active learning and high-throughput experiments for oxidative coupling of methane. Of 36 selected catalysts, 30 reached combined ethane and ethylene yields of at least 15% in the reported tests. This is a small-data, reaction-specific catalyst screening outcome; the paper also tests feature engineering on other catalysis datasets. A ChemRxiv version predates the journal publication, and this record does not claim journal-version priority.
ai_technology: Automatic feature engineering with active learning
organization: Japan Advanced Institute of Science and Technology; Hokkaido University

source_review.scope: Full published article text in German National Library repository and publisher-indexed primary metadata/abstract; earlier ChemRxiv version noted but not compared.

evidence.tested: The article reports 36 selected oxidative coupling of methane catalysts experimentally assessed; 30 achieved combined ethane and ethylene yields of at least 15% under the reported test conditions.
evidence.unknown: The paper also appeared as an earlier ChemRxiv version; this check did not establish whether every quantitative detail appeared in that version. The result is limited to the reported catalyst set and reaction conditions.
evidence.ai_role: Automatic feature engineering extracted catalyst descriptors, and active learning selected catalysts for high-throughput experimental testing.
